title: Explainability Bridge: Interactive Decision Canvas for Cache & Batch Policies
creator: Dana Chen
description:
Goal: Ship a lightweight, interactive "Explainability Bridge" in Redwood Console that lets operators understand and safely apply recommended caching + batching policies. The Bridge is a decision canvas that ties recommendations to measurable outcomes (cost delta, p95 latency, cache hit rate) and to sample request archetypes so users can see concrete examples of how a policy change will affect their traffic.

Hypothesis: Exposing the "why" (model/traffic signals, confidence, trade-offs) and attaching simple rollback guardrails will increase adoption of optimizer recommendations and reduce operator friction when tuning reserved and hosted workloads.

Key deliverables:
- Full-screen Canvas: policy cards plotted along two axes (cost savings vs. latency risk) with confidence bands and ability to filter by endpoint/model/region.
- Why Panel: per-recommendation rationale (signals used, simulated token-level impact, example requests) with inline microcopy templates for admin-facing change logs.
- Simulation Mode: run recommendations against a sampled trace to show per-route delta and 95% CI for latency and cost; store simulation runs in timeline.
- Rollout Controls: canary slice generator (percent + route selectors), automatic fallback triggers (latency > 10% p95 or error-rate breach), and one-click rollback playbook.
- Audit & Explain: attach human-readable justification to changes plus links to the evaluation run and the PR that will carry server-side changes.

Success metrics: adoption of recommended presets (>= 25% of non-enterprise routes within 2 cycles), drop in manual rollback incidents, and improved confidence (measured via in-product survey).
comments: 2026-02-12 — Dana Chen: Initial sketch uploaded to Figma. Focused on horizontal policy cards seeded from Optimize's recommendation engine. Called out need for example request sampling to make impact concrete.

2026-02-16 — Marco Ruiz: Eng sync: backend will expose a sampled-trace endpoint and a deterministic simulator; ENG team flagged throughput cost for on-demand sim runs — suggested precomputing nightly sims for high-volume routes.

2026-02-18 — Aisha Patel (PM): Love the 'Why Panel' idea. Request: add a short 'confidence meter' and link to the eval case that produced the recommendation. Also requested a path to mark recommendations as 'not applicable' with a reason for audit logs.

2026-02-20 — Nora Singh (Eng Reviewer): Security note: any stored sample traces must be scrubbed of PII and tied to retention policy. Suggest KMS tagging for audit. Also noted that rollback triggers should be evaluated server-side, not just UI-side enforcement.

2026-02-22 — User Research (Kumar Rao): Quick hallway testing with three infra operators — feedback: operators wanted a compact diff view that shows token-level delta for a single representative request; they were wary of 'savings' numbers without distributional context.

2026-02-25 — Marco Ruiz: Design/Eng trade-off: full-fidelity simulation is expensive. Decision: support both 'fast sim' (statistical approximation) in UI for iterative exploration and 'full sim' as an async job with notification when ready. Added ticket ENG-41988 for simulator infra work.

2026-02-27 — Dana Chen: Updated prototype with canary slice modal and rollback playbook checklist. Added microcopy suggestions for change logs: 'Why we changed this: lower per-token cost for routing group X; confidence: medium (based on 14K samples)'.

2026-03-01 — Design Review (cross-functional): Feedback accepted with minor tweaks — clarify that recommendations are suggestions, not enforced; add explicit 'require approval' toggle for enterprise tenants. Action: create follow-up PM ticket for approval flow and add security checklist.
